title: Net Stable Funding Ratio, LCR and Leverage Ratio
vardeezReading: ORR-22: untiered by Vardeez, with the note that his themes "Stressed market VaR (calculations)" and "Basel 2.5 market risk calculation" land squarely here and the reading should be treated as high priority. ORR-23: Very Important.

los.vardeez: Basel III liquidity and leverage ratios

selectors.name: NSFR from ASF and RSF factors
selectors.what: NSFR = ASF / RSF, where ASF = sum of (liability or equity amount x ASF factor) and RSF = sum of (asset amount x RSF factor), from a balance sheet with the factors given; compliant when at least 1.
selectors.theory: What each side measures and why: ASF weights liabilities and equity by how stable the funding is over a stressful one-year horizon (equity and long bonds 100%, stable retail deposits 95%, short wholesale CDs 0%), RSF weights assets by how illiquid they are (vault cash 0%, business loans over one year 85%); the ratio is ASF over RSF, not the inverse.

selectors.name: NSFR shortfall: new funding needed
selectors.what: The amount of new funding needed to bring NSFR to 100%, counting both legs: the funding adds ASF and its deployment into an asset adds RSF, so ASF + a x X = RSF + r x X and X = (RSF - ASF) / (a - r).
selectors.theory: Why the gap cannot be divided by the ASF factor alone: the new funding is invested in an asset that itself carries an RSF factor, so only the difference a - r closes the gap.

selectors.name: NSFR versus LCR: pick the right factors
selectors.what: A table gives both parameter sets (ASF and RSF factors for the NSFR; HQLA factors and run-off rates for the LCR); the question asks for NSFR = ASF / RSF or LCR = HQLA / net cash outflows over 30 days, and the right factors must be taken for the ratio asked.
selectors.theory: The two ratios differ in horizon and purpose: LCR is 30 days, liquid assets against stressed outflows (short-term resilience); NSFR is one year, available against required stable funding (structural). HQLA factors are not RSF factors (cash: HQLA 100%, RSF 0%) and LCR run-off rates are not ASF factors.

selectors.name: Leverage ratio calculation
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Basel III liquidity and leverage ratios'; LO f: calculate the required leverage ratio
selectors.what: Leverage ratio = Core Tier 1 capital / Leverage Exposure, at least 3%, with the exposure including on-balance-sheet assets and fractions of off-balance-sheet items; also the G-SIB leverage buffer of 50% of the risk-weighted G-SIB higher-loss absorbency requirement, met with Tier 1 capital.
selectors.theory: The leverage ratio is a simple capital measure on unweighted exposure that supplements, not replaces, risk-based requirements; it is not a liquidity ratio.

notSelected: ORR-22 f's background (why leverage and liquidity requirements exist, Northern Rock, HQLA levels, the LCR run-off assumptions beyond the figures given in a question) and ORR-23 b's 2017 leverage ratio framework details (exposure measure refinements, central bank reserve exemption, buffer ranges, earlier US rule) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer beyond what S1 to S3 and V1 cover.
